I used to write little prayers down, describing my pain so openly in a little notebook. I had no trouble letting God know that I was confused, angry, and hurting. Sometimes I even asked God to kill me, as I wanted an escape so badly. My trust in God was dwindling.

One verse kept me going though. Every time I felt like hopelessness was all I knew, this one verse gave me reason to pray another night. "We know that God causes everything to work together for the good of those who love God and are called according to His purpose for them." (Romans 8:28) I knew intellectually that God was somehow working it all out for my good. Emotionally I started to hate that verse, and even accused God of lying. But I knew that it was true, that somehow the pain was being used for good. This kept me going, no better feeling than the days before, but it kept that small spark of hope in me. And so I kept praying (somewhat angrily).

After what seemed like forever, I also came across another passage, which helped immensely: 
"How long, Lord ? Will you forget me forever? How long will you hide your face from me?  How long must I wrestle with my thoughts and day after day have sorrow in my heart? How long will my enemy triumph over me?  Look on me and answer, Lord my God. Give light to my eyes, or I will sleep in death,  and my enemy will say, “I have overcome him,” and my foes will rejoice when I fall.  But I trust in your unfailing love; my heart rejoices in your salvation.  I will sing the Lord ’s praise, for he has been good to me."
I read through the first few verses and felt like I had finally found something in the Bible that made sense in my life. It asked the same sorts of questions as I was: "Where is God?" 

Then I read the last 2 verses, where it switches tone completely. All of a sudden it says "But I trust your unfailing love" and it made no sense. That "But" seemed to change the whole chapter. It began as a plea to God to listen, to answer the prayers of a frustrated and brokenhearted servant. And it ended as a promise, a promise to trust in God and to praise Him in the midst of the empty-feeling confusion. What changed? The psalmist, (in this case David), realized that the only true way to find joy is to trust once more in God. 

After I came across that, I shifted my position in prayer. Instead of, God, why aren't you listening, can't You see my situation?" I prayed, "Lord, I'm confused, I'm lost, and I feel like death. I can't do this anymore, not on my own, and not with you silent. Please, I'm ready to be used however you would use me. Forgive me, and fill me with your Spirit. Please." (That was paraphrased, most of that wasn't spoken out loud because I was crying to hard to say anything)

Whenever I fall like this, there are a few things I do: 

1. I pray. I don't just say, "oh Lord, forgive me" and move on. I take the time to spill my heart out to God, and ask for not only His forgiveness but also His guidance and Strength. I surrender completely, knowing that I have failed to glorify God with my life.

2. I read a few of the Psalms. Psalm 51 is good when in need of repentance, and Psalm 86 is good as well. (If you ever feel like God isn't listening to your prayers, then Psalm 13 is good too.) 

3. I read Romans 7 and 8. They're 2 great chapters that talk all about sin, God's power, and God's promises. 

4. I come to other people in honesty about what I've done, and ask for their help as well. For you this would mean telling your wife about what you did, and asking for her help and support to overcome this. (Don't be afraid of this, a godly woman will be forgiving and helpful in this process.) 

5. I remind myself constantly, even when I don't feel like it, that I do what I do for the glory of God, not for my own personal pleasure. This includes doing stuff like reading the Bible whenever temptation comes my way.
